clues.text: This town stands by the sea where a stream runs out to meet it. A town named Sale sits on the far bank, right across the stream.
clues.narrowing: Puts the player on an Atlantic river mouth in northwest Africa.

source.quote: Rabat is located on the Atlantic Ocean at the mouth of the river Bou Regreg, opposite Salé, the city's main commuter town.

clues.text: By the sea, this town has hot, dry days in the warm months of the year. The cold months stay mild, with damp air and soft rain at times.
clues.narrowing: Keeps a mild Atlantic-coast capital with dry summers and damp winters.

source.quote: Rabat features a hot-summer Mediterranean climate (Csa) with warm to hot, dry summers and mild, damp winters.

clues.text: In 1956 this land won its freedom and stood on its own. This town was then made the chief town of the free land.
clues.narrowing: Shrinks the list to capitals confirmed at independence in 1956.

source.quote: When Morocco achieved independence in 1956, Rabat became its capital.

clues.text: A huge tower here is the minaret of a mosque that was never finished. It has stood watch over the river shore for more than 800 years.
clues.narrowing: Nearly decisive: one capital's landmark is an unfinished minaret by a river.

source.quote: Overlooking the shores of the river is the Hassan Tower, a monumental unfinished minaret constructed by Ya'qub al-Mansur in the late 12th century.

clues.text: The men and women who lead Morocco work in this town, by the sea shore. It is the seat of rule for the whole wide land.
clues.narrowing: Confirms it: the capital city of Morocco.

source.quote: Rabat is the capital city of Morocco, located on the northwestern coasts of the Atlantic Ocean.

reveal.blurb: Sultans built a fortress city here in the 1100s, and pirates later sailed from its river. Its great Hassan Tower was meant for a giant mosque that was never finished. Rabat is the capital of Morocco.
